challenge.reason: The old decision's stated rationale (fewer than 20 issues per run, simplicity of one atomic file) is invalidated by concrete changes: runs of 200+ issues and a concurrency executor writing issues in parallel. The new design addresses the two named failure modes (single-lock contention on heartbeat and status writes, one corrupt byte losing the whole run) and keeps the same directory root with an index file for discovery. The supersession argument is sound. Implementation should still make each per-issue write and the index update atomic (write-then-rename), but that is a build concern, not a flaw in the supersession case.
